title: Expert interviews with professionals from healthcare research and design as well as from healthcare practice on barriers, facilitators, good practices and recommendations for action in cancer screening for people with intellectual disabilities as part of the EUCanScreen Joint Action
summary: In Germany, many people live with an intellectual disability. They develop cancer about as often as the general population, but they face greater difficulties in accessing preventive and early detection examinations. This is especially true for colorectal, cervical, and breast cancer screening. As a result, cancers are often detected at a later stage. In this project, we want to explore which barriers exist, but also which approaches work well. To do so, we interview experts from different European countries, for example doctors, researchers, or representatives of advocacy organisations. The aim is to develop recommendations to improve access to cancer screening for people with intellectual disabilities.
conditions: People with intellectual disabilities according to ICD-10 (F70–F79). In addition, syndromes associated with ID are included, such as Rett syndrome (F84.2), encephalocele (Q01), microcephaly (Q02), Down syndrome (Q90), Edwards and Patau syndromes (Q91), other trisomies (Q92), and Fragile X syndrome (Q99.2).

interventions.name: Experts from research, programme design, and clinical practice who will be interviewed on barriers, facilitators, good practices, and recommendations in cancer screening for people with intellectual disabilities.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
a) Experts from at least one of the following areas:
- Clinical care (e.g. physicians, nurses)
- Health policy, health research, professional association or scientific society
- Advocacy for people with intellectual disabilities
b) Relevant experience in at least one of the following areas:
- Design, implementation, or evaluation of cancer screening programmes
- Work with people with intellectual disabilities

Participants (experts) come from various European countries; however, recruitment, interviews, coordination, and data analysis are carried out exclusively by the German Cancer Society in Berlin, Germany.
Exclusion criteria:
Persons without relevant background in these areas
